messages:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding run for magnet-48k-int4v2 showed a reproducible RoPE overshoot / context bleed around token ~29.4k on longprefill tests. attaching short repro and sample mismatch.
jonathan: Can you paste the minimal repro and the model tag you used?
maya: Model: magnet-48k@v1.2-quant-int4v2, deploy: canary-dedicated-us-west2. Repro command:
```bash
python tests/repro_longctx.py --model magnet-48k@v1.2 --quant int4v2 --context 32768 --prompt-file tests/long_30k.txt
```
Output diff excerpt (quant vs fp16):
```
--- fp16
... "The meeting concluded with a vote" ...
+++ int4v2
... "The meeting concluded with a vote\nThe meeting concluded with a vote" ...
```
li: Oof duplicate tail tokens — looks like KV-cache read is returning stale positions (index wrap?). Do you have the token index dump when it happens?
maya: Pasted small dump below (token idx arrays truncated):
```
kv_pos: [29290,29291,29292,...,32767,0,1,2]
kv_seq: [..]
last_index_seen: 32770
```
sasha: That kv_pos wrap after 32767 is suspicious — our circular buffer size for 32k should clamp/offset, not let absolute positions roll into 0..n without remapping. Did quant alter memcpy/pad leading to off-by-one in prefill stride?
eli: Quick sanity: does fp16 run the exact same prefill sequence? If fp16 maps positions with the same codepath, it might be a quant-specific pointer math bug. Try running `--quant int8` and `--quant int4v1` to compare.
maya: Ran int8 and int4v1 locally:
- fp16: PASS (no duplicate tail)
- int8: PASS
- int4v1: FAIL (same symptom)
So fail surface correlates with older int4-style packing and int4v2.
ci-bot: [test-run] 4412345678-repro: canary-dedicated-us-west2 job finished — logs @ https://ci.internal/runs/4412345678
jonathan: Sounds like a packing/memcopy path for packed 4-bit tensors is stomping KV index table on wrap. Two likely spots: the prefill memcpy when shard boundaries cross or the SIMD gather that writes offsets.
li: Can you capture a small reproducer that uses a synthetic prompt that deterministicly triggers at N=29000 so we don't need full 30k file? I can run local memory watchpoints.
maya: Created synthetic trigger script: 
```python
# make_trigger.py
from token_utils import repeat_tok
prompt = repeat_tok("\nA\n", 29290) + "Summary:" 
# writes to tests/synth_29k.txt
```
I'll drop it in tests/ and kick a run with --trace-kv=1
sasha: Also add an env var to disable KV-cache ring remap to see if behaviour changes: `REDWOOD_KV_REMAP=0` — if that disables remap and suddenly no dupes then remap code is culprit.
eli: I'll queue a bisect: quant packing code changes from patch 0xa1..0xb4. If this reproduces locally I can narrow to the memcpy rewrite that landed in int4v2.
maya: Running with `--trace-kv` now, attaching short trace when done. Also captured the binary blob of kv_pos before/after memcpy.
jonathan: Thanks — once trace is up ping me, I'll try scoped repro on dedicated hw (to rule out CPU->GPU memcpy differences). If reproducible on dedicated I'll open a rollback PR for the packing path.
maya: Trace snippet (trimmed):
```
TRACE: prefill memcpy dst=0x7ff... len=8192 shard=3
TRACE: kv_pos before=[32760,32761,32762,32763,32764,32765,32766,32767]
TRACE: memcpy src overlap -> dst overwritten with [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]
```
ci-bot: [analysis] 4412345678: memory-overlap pattern matched known bug template "packed-memcpy-wrap-2026-03"; suggested label: regression/kv-index
li: If confirmed, short-term mitigation: clamp remap logic to use modulo arithmetic on absolute position and add assertion when prefill length crosses shard boundary.
maya: Agree. I'll open a draft PR with a failing test and the mitigation clamp + extra assertion. Assigning to @jonathan and @eli for review.
jonathan: Good plan. @eli can you also add a small fuzz harness for quant packing so CI catches regression next time?
eli: Yep on it. Will add an int4 packing fuzz job that runs on PRs for models >16k context.
maya: Thx all. I'll update this thread with the failing test link and PR once ready. :eyes:
jonathan: :thumbsup:
ci-bot: [note] Created issue #ML-2123 "RoPE overshoot due to packed memcpy wrap" from thread 4412345678"
maya: Filed PR draft: https://git.internal/r/PR/12345 (tests failing)
sasha: Nice repro, thanks. Keep the synthetic prompt in tests so we have deterministic regression coverage.
maya: Will do. Closing for now, will reopen if new artifacts show up."
